- **White pith** visible in the interior
- Dark brown discoloration along vascular tissue/edges
- Stem is bleached/dried externally
- No fluffy mold or black sclerotia

The white pith is a critical diagnostic feature. Per the symptom descriptions: "SDS-infected plants have white pith when stems are cut, distinguishing it from brown stem rot which causes brown pith discoloration."

Top candidate: **Sudden_death_syndrome** (white pith + vascular discoloration). Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference leaf image shows SDS foliar symptoms (interveinal chlorosis with green veins remaining). The test image shows the stem cross-section aspect of SDS - which is specifically characterized by **white pith** when stems are split, contrasted with brown pith in Brown Stem Rot.

The white pith with dark vascular discoloration in the split stem is a textbook SDS diagnostic feature per the knowledge base: "SDS-infected plants have white pith when stems are cut, distinguishing it from brown stem rot which causes brown pith discoloration."
